conflicts.statement: Release from the SIN sector is 18:40Z on 3 Nov and report for MAD-FCO is 04:40Z on 4 Nov — exactly 10h00. With your 85-minute commute at each end, that leaves 7h10 of uninterrupted sleep opportunity, not the required 8h. I have planned 6h15 of actual sleep, which is all that fits once you allow time to fall asleep.
options: Notify the operator under 117.25(f) before you report — the regulation puts this determination on you, and once you make it you cannot report until you've had a rest period that does give 8 uninterrupted hours.
Ask crewing to push the 4 Nov report by at least 50 minutes (to 05:30Z / 06:30 local), which would give 10h50 rest and clear the 8-hour opportunity.
Ask to be released from the 4 Nov MAD-FCO-MAD turn entirely; it is a 7h08 duty sitting between a 15h30 SIN sector and a 05:00 standby.

If you go, take an airport hotel or crashpad at MAD for the night of 3 Nov — that recovers roughly 2h50 of the commute and gets you close to 9h in bed, though it does not change the regulatory finding.

conflicts.statement: The rest at base between 3 Nov and 4 Nov is 10h00, two hours short of the operator's 12-hour standard at base.
options: Raise it with crewing alongside the 8-hour sleep opportunity point — the same delay or removal fixes both.
File a fatigue report on the pairing so the 3-4 Nov junction gets looked at for future months.

conflicts.statement: Your own line is 9 hours between getting home and leaving again. On the night of 3-4 Nov you are through the door at about 20:05Z and back out at 03:15Z — 7h10. By your own rule, going home is not worth it.
options: Stay near MAD for that one night rather than commuting, and keep the 9-hour rule intact for the rest of the month.
Move your own line down to 7 hours for this single night — your call, nobody else's.
Decline the 4 Nov duty and the question disappears.

conflicts.statement: MAD-SIN is 15h30 from 10:10Z report to 01:40Z release, and the 13h30 block on its own already exceeds the operator's 13-hour planned FDP ceiling.
options: Confirm with crewing that this is planned as an augmented crew with in-flight rest, which is what would normally extend the FDP beyond 13 hours — if so the Flight Crew Manual figure is the wrong one to read it against.
If it is not augmented, query the pairing before the roster goes firm — this is the same shape on 31 Oct, 1 Nov and 3 Nov, so it is four duties, not one.
Plan your in-flight rest slot with the other crew at briefing; I have not scheduled any sleep inside the duty because that is a cockpit decision on the day, not a calendar entry.

conflicts.statement: SIN-MAD is 15h30 from 00:45Z report to 16:15Z release, over the 13-hour planned FDP ceiling.
options: Same query as 29 Oct — establish whether the pairing is crewed as augmented.
Note that this duty starts at your circadian low and runs 15h30; if you arrive at report already short, call it before you sign on rather than after.

conflicts.statement: MAD-SIN is 15h30 from 13:35Z report to 05:05Z release, over the 13-hour planned FDP ceiling.
options: Same query as 29 Oct — establish whether the pairing is crewed as augmented.

conflicts.statement: SIN-MAD is 15h30 from 03:10Z report to 18:40Z release, over the 13-hour planned FDP ceiling — and it is the duty that feeds straight into the 10-hour rest before 4 Nov.
options: Same query as 29 Oct — establish whether the pairing is crewed as augmented.
This is the strongest single case for getting the 4 Nov turn moved or dropped: a 15h30 duty followed by a 10h00 rest and a 05:40 report is the worst junction in the month.
